interest: This file provides an extraordinary, granular view of U.S.-Japanese financial relations and bureaucratic maneuvering during the crucial months immediately preceding the July 26, 1941 freezing order and the outbreak of the Pacific War. It illuminates the intersection between state-level insurance regulation (the New York State Insurance Department under Louis H. Pink) and federal foreign economic policy (Herbert Feis, Dean Acheson, and the Division of Far Eastern Affairs). The documents reveal Japanese firms systematically liquidating holdings, reinsuring policies with American companies like Aetna, and seeking to repatriate millions of dollars in surplus capital. Crucially, the correspondence captures the State Department's dramatic pivot from strict non-intervention and reluctance to discriminate against Japan in late 1940 and May 1941 to an urgent, informal effort in early July 1941 to stall a $1,000,000 transfer by Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Company just weeks before total economic warfare was declared.
overview: This decimal file (894.506 Insurance) documents communications between New York State Superintendent of Insurance Louis H. Pink and officials of the U.S. Department of State—principally Adviser on International Economic Affairs Herbert Feis, Assistant Secretary Dean Acheson, and the Division of Far Eastern Affairs—between December 1940 and July 1941 concerning the liquidation and repatriation of Japanese and Italian insurance assets. Throughout late 1940 and May 1941, New York insurance authorities permitted the release of millions of dollars in surplus and free funds to Japanese companies (notably the Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Company, Ltd.) and oversaw stock transactions with American firms such as Aetna Insurance Company, with the State Department repeatedly declining to intervene. However, as tensions mounted and American assets in Japan were increasingly restricted, internal debates within the State Department weighed capital controls and bilateral negotiations against concerns about discriminatory treatment. By early July 1941, on the eve of the United States freezing all Japanese assets, State Department policy pivoted sharply, culminating in an urgent request to Superintendent Pink to find any way to stall and defer a pending $1,000,000 remittance by Tokio Marine for several weeks.

subfiles.about: Notification by the New York Superintendent of Insurance regarding the pending release of approximately $1.5 million to two Japanese insurance companies.
subfiles.from: Louis H. Pink, Superintendent of Insurance, State of New York
subfiles.summary: Superintendent Louis H. Pink writes to Herbert Feis to give notice that the New York Insurance Department is about to release approximately $1,500,000 to two Japanese insurance companies. Pink notes that according to previous correspondence and conversations, the State Department had no objection. He explains that he is notifying the Department to ensure circumstances have not changed, and will proceed unless he receives a prompt objection.
subfiles.title: Letter from Louis H. Pink to Herbert Feis on release of funds to Japanese companies
subfiles.to: Herbert Feis, Adviser on International Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: State Department response declining to comment on the release of funds to two Japanese insurance companies.
subfiles.from: Herbert Feis, Adviser on International Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Herbert Feis acknowledges Louis H. Pink's letter of December 20, 1940, concerning the intended release of approximately $1.5 million to two Japanese insurance companies. Feis thanks the Superintendent for providing the information to the Department of State. However, he explicitly states that the Department does not desire to comment concerning the transaction.
subfiles.title: Letter from Herbert Feis to Louis H. Pink declining comment on Japanese fund release
subfiles.to: Louis H. Pink, Superintendent of Insurance of the State of New York

subfiles.about: Policy recommendation by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs on general versus discriminatory capital controls against Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Division of Far Eastern Affairs comments on underlying memoranda and a draft letter to the New York Superintendent of Insurance concerning Japanese assets in the United States. FE agrees that controlling capital transfers from the United States to Japan is desirable. However, it strongly suggests that any such control be merged into general action covering all countries or groups of countries to avoid singling out Japan for discriminatory action.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Division of Far Eastern Affairs on capital transfer controls
subfiles.to: Dean Acheson, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Recommendation by Herbert Feis to exercise exchange controls over capital transfers to Japan and initiate negotiations.
subfiles.from: Herbert Feis, Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Herbert Feis warns that pending transactions represent further substantial steps in the liquidation of Japanese assets within the United States. In light of increasing Japanese restrictions on American assets in Japan, Feis recommends that the U.S. government exercise control over capital transfers to Japan. He also recommends immediately notifying Japan of U.S. readiness to negotiate an agreement governing bilateral capital transfers.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Herbert Feis recommending control over capital transfers to Japan
subfiles.to: Dean Acheson, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Detailed review and analysis of New York Insurance Department inquiries concerning Japanese and Italian fund releases and stock transactions.
subfiles.from: George F. Luthringer, Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: George F. Luthringer reviews Superintendent Pink's letter requesting Department views on the release of $1,000,000 to a Japanese insurance company and $100,000 to an Italian company, alongside proposed stock transfers to Aetna Insurance Company that would release $7,000,000 to $7,500,000 to Japan. Luthringer notes that because the Department previously declined to comment on transactions involving $7.5 million and $500,000, it will likely not comment on the present request. A handwritten note by Herbert Feis reiterates support for exchange controls and a negotiated agreement while U.S. assets remain frozen in Japan.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from George F. Luthringer on Japanese and Italian insurance company requests

subfiles.about: Inquiry from the New York Insurance Department regarding upcoming releases of funds to Japanese and Italian insurance companies.
subfiles.from: Louis H. Pink, Superintendent of Insurance, State of New York
subfiles.summary: Louis H. Pink writes to Herbert Feis stating that New York expects shortly to release another $1,000,000 to a Japanese insurance company because the funds are not required to protect U.S. creditors. He also reports an Italian company's request to release $100,000 and reorganize by selling stock to American interests, which would transfer considerable capital to Italian hands. Pink offers to meet in Washington for discussion and notes he will permit withdrawals if no objections are received.
subfiles.title: Letter from Louis H. Pink to Herbert Feis regarding proposed Japanese and Italian fund releases
subfiles.to: Herbert Feis, Adviser on International Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: State Department response declining comment on specific releases of Japanese and Italian insurance funds while requesting notice of future cases.
subfiles.from: Herbert Feis, Adviser on International Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Herbert Feis replies to Louis H. Pink's letter of May 16, 1941, thanking him for requesting the Department's views and offering to travel to Washington. Feis conveys that the Department does not desire to comment concerning the specific Japanese and Italian transactions under reference. However, he requests that the Department be afforded an opportunity to express its views if similar requests for releasing funds or selling stock arise in the future.
subfiles.title: Letter from Herbert Feis to Louis H. Pink declining comment on specific fund withdrawals
subfiles.to: Louis H. Pink, Superintendent of Insurance, State of New York

subfiles.about: Notice of an application by Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Company to remit $1,000,000 from free funds to Japan.
subfiles.from: Louis H. Pink, Superintendent of Insurance, State of New York
subfiles.summary: Superintendent Pink informs Herbert Feis that Appleton & Cox, Inc., attorneys for Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Company, Ltd., have applied to remit $1,000,000 from the company's free funds. Pink explains that Tokio has reinsured most of its business in American companies, retaining only marine business with liabilities slightly over $1,000,000 against more than $3,000,000 in free funds and adequate trusteed surplus. Pink states he must permit the withdrawal in good faith unless advised otherwise, and holds consent for a few days to permit State Department review.
subfiles.title: Letter from Louis H. Pink to Herbert Feis on Tokio Marine & Fire application to remit $1,000,000
subfiles.to: Herbert Feis, Adviser on International Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Recommendation to authorize requesting New York insurance authorities to defer Tokio Marine's $1,000,000 remittance for several weeks.
subfiles.summary: The Division of Far Eastern Affairs submits a memorandum to Under Secretary of State Sumner Welles regarding the pending Tokio Marine transaction. FE suggests that Welles authorize the Adviser on International Economic Affairs (EA) to inform the New York Superintendent of Insurance that the Department would appreciate his deferring action on the $1,000,000 remittance application for several weeks if any way can be found to do so.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Division of Far Eastern Affairs to Sumner Welles recommending deferral of Tokio Marine remittance
subfiles.to: Sumner Welles, Under Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Internal State Department inquiry querying whether there is any objection to the Tokio Marine remittance based on precedent.
subfiles.summary: An internal routing slip from GC in the Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs asks whether the Department maintains its previous posture. The handwritten or typed query asks: "I suppose that in line with previous cases there is no objection?"
subfiles.title: Routing note from Adviser on International Economic Affairs to Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: State Department request asking the New York Superintendent of Insurance to defer action on Tokio Marine's remittance application.
subfiles.from: Herbert Feis, Adviser on International Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Replying to Louis H. Pink's letter of June 30, Herbert Feis informs the Superintendent that the Department of State would appreciate it if any way could be found to defer action for several weeks on the application of the Tokyo Marine & Fire Insurance Company. This letter represents an active federal intervention to hold Japanese capital in the United States immediately prior to the comprehensive freezing order of late July 1941.
subfiles.title: Letter from Herbert Feis to Louis H. Pink requesting deferral of Tokyo Marine remittance
subfiles.to: Louis H. Pink, Superintendent of Insurance, State of New York
